    K-mer features from sequences

    Source: R/recipes-steps.R
    step_bio_kmers.Rd

    step_bio_kmers() creates a specification of a recipe step that turns a column of DNA, RNA or protein sequences into k-mer count or frequency features. The k-mer vocabulary is learnt from the training set when the recipe is prepped, so new data always get the same columns.

    Usage

    step_bio_kmers(
  recipe,
  ...,
  role = "predictor",
  trained = FALSE,
  k = 3,
  normalise = TRUE,
  vocabulary = NULL,
  keep_original_cols = FALSE,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = recipes::rand_id("bio_kmers")
)

# S3 method for class 'step_bio_kmers'
tidy(x, ...)

    Arguments

    recipe

    A recipe object. The step is added to its sequence of operations.

    ...

    One or more selector functions to choose sequence columns. See recipes::selections().

    role

    Role for the new feature columns.

    trained

    A logical showing whether the step has been trained.

    k

    K-mer length.

    normalise

    If TRUE (the default), use k-mer frequencies rather than counts, which removes the effect of sequence length.

    vocabulary

    The learnt k-mers, one character vector per column. Filled in by recipes::prep().

    keep_original_cols

    Keep the original sequence columns?

    skip

    Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by recipes::bake()?

    id

    A character string that is unique to this step.

    x

    A step_bio_kmers object.

    Value

    An updated version of recipe with the new step added. When you tidy() this step, a tibble with columns terms, k and n_kmers is returned.

    See also

    Other tidybiotek recipe steps: step_bio_aa_props(), step_bio_vst_norm()

    Examples

    rec <- recipes::recipe(gc ~ sequence, data = bio_gc_content(ecoli_cds, sequence)) |>
  step_bio_kmers(sequence, k = 2) |>
  recipes::prep()
recipes::bake(rec, new_data = NULL)
#> # A tibble: 76 × 17
